claims.claim: Recent Western nuclear builds have completed at costs in the mid-to-high teens of billions of dollars per gigawatt: Vogtle units 3-4 cost $36.8 billion for two ~1.1 GW AP1000 reactors (~$16-17bn/GW).
claims.episode_span: whose completed costs have run in the mid-to-high teens of billions of dollars per gigawatt
claims.supporting_quote: Construction cost Units 1–2: $8.87 billion (1989 USD) [ 1 ] ($19.5 billion in 2024 dollars [ 2 ] ) Units 3–4: $36.8 Billion

claims.claim: Licensing consumes years before construction: Vogtle's combined construction and operating license was applied for in March 2008 and approved by the NRC in February 2012 -- about four years -- consistent with the digest's four-to-ten-year range.
claims.episode_span: the extended licensing and permitting timeline, which can consume four to ten years before first concrete
claims.supporting_quote: In February 2012, the NRC approved the construction license of the two proposed AP1000 reactors at Vogtle

claims.claim: A gigawatt-scale reactor's bulk material inputs are tens of thousands of tonnes of steel and on the order of two hundred thousand cubic meters of concrete (a standard figure is under 40 t steel and 190 m3 concrete per MW).
claims.episode_span: Commodity steel might total on the order of twenty to thirty thousand tonnes
claims.source_title: Constructing a lot of nuclear power plants is not material constrained | NextBigFuture.com
claims.supporting_quote: Modern nuclear reactors need less than 40 metric tons of steel and 190 cubic meters of concrete per megawatt of average capacity

claims.claim: Financing cost on a nuclear build is interest on capital dictated by the construction period, and long construction periods have pushed up financing costs very significantly.
claims.episode_span: Carrying costs on capital compound at several percent per year across the full schedule
claims.source_title: Economics of Nuclear Power - World Nuclear Association

claims.claim: Long construction periods have historically pushed up nuclear financing costs very significantly, supporting the digest's claim that multi-year delays compound the interest burden.
claims.episode_span: turning a five-year delay into an effective doubling of the interest burden
